Test Case 1: Display the Welcome Screen
Verify that launching Safe Voice displays the welcome screen with the application name, purpose, and Proceed to Report button.
Safe Voice is installed on a compatible Android device or emulator.
2. Wait for the initial screen to load.
The welcome screen displays the Safe Voice name, a brief explanation of the application purpose, and the Proceed to Report button.
The application remains on the welcome screen; no report has been created.
Test Case 2: Begin Reporting Without an Account
Verify that a reporter can begin the reporting workflow without creating an account or logging in.
2. Observe the next screen or reporting step.
The reporting workflow opens without requiring account registration or reporter login.
The reporter can continue through the reporting workflow without an account.
Test Case 3: Select the Reporting Context
Verify that a reporter can indicate whether the incident happened to them or whether they are reporting on behalf of someone else.
The reporter has entered the reporting workflow.
Reporting context: reporting on behalf of someone else.
2. Select the option indicating that the report is being made on behalf of someone else.
The selected reporting context is accepted and the workflow allows the reporter to continue.
The chosen reporting context is retained for the current report.
Test Case 4: Continue Without Selecting a Reporting Context
Verify that the application identifies a missing reporting-context selection when that selection is required to continue.
The reporter is on the reporting-context step.
2. Attempt to continue to the next step.
The application indicates that the reporting context needs attention and does not silently record an unselected choice.
The reporter remains at the reporting-context step until the required choice is made.
Test Case 5: Submit a Report Without Personal Contact Details
Verify that a valid report can be submitted without requiring the reporter to provide a name, phone number, email address, or account details.
The reporting workflow is available and the report can be saved in the test environment.
Category: Domestic Violence; Description: Fictional test report for Safe Voice; Name: blank; Phone: blank; Email: blank.
2. Enter the required incident information using the test data.
3. Leave reporter name and contact details blank and do not create an account.

The application does not block submission merely because reporter identity or contact details were not provided; after a successful save, it displays the submission confirmation and case reference number.
A fictional test report is saved without mandatory reporter identity/contact details.
Test Case 6: Select a GBV Incident Category
Verify that a reporter can select a valid GBV incident category for a report.
The reporter is on the incident-information step.
Domestic Violence is accepted as the selected incident category and is associated with the report.
The selected category remains available in the report being prepared.
Test Case 7: Submit Without an Incident Category
Verify that the application prevents submission when the required incident category has not been selected.
The reporter is preparing a report and the incident category is a required field in the UI.
Incident category: not selected; Description: Fictional test report.
2. Enter the other required test information.
The application identifies the missing required category and does not show a successful-submission confirmation or case reference number.
No report is confirmed as successfully submitted.
Test Case 8: Enter an Incident Description
Verify that a reporter can enter a description of the incident in the report form.
Description: Fictional test report created only to check the Safe Voice form.
3. Move to the next step or review the report.
The description is accepted and remains visible when the reporter reviews the report information.
The report draft contains the entered description.
Test Case 9: Submit Without an Incident Description
Verify that the application validates a missing incident description when the description is required.
The reporter is preparing a report and the incident description is a required field in the UI.
Incident category: Physical Abuse; Description: blank.
The application identifies the missing required description and does not confirm that the report was saved.
The reporter can correct the description; no successful submission is recorded.
Test Case 10: Enter Known Incident Date, Time, and Location
Verify that a reporter can provide the incident date, time, and location when those details are known.
Incident date: 20/10/2026; Incident time: 14:30; Incident location: Test Location A (fictional).
The entered date, time, and incident location are retained with the report. The incident location is treated separately from the reporter’s current device location.
The report draft contains the supplied incident details.
Test Case 11: Leave Unknown Incident Details Blank
Verify that the reporting workflow can accommodate incident date, time, or location details that the reporter does not know.
The reporter is preparing a report and has entered the required incident information.
Incident date: unknown; Incident time: unknown; Incident location: unknown; Category and description: supplied.
1. Enter a valid incident category and description.
2. Leave incident date, time, and location blank because they are unknown.
The application does not require the reporter to invent incident details that are not known; required fields are still validated and submission follows the UI rules.
Unknown incident details remain blank rather than being replaced by the reporter’s current location or guessed values.
Test Case 12: Attach Optional Supporting Evidence
Verify that a reporter can attach a supported evidence file to a report when evidence is available.
Evidence attachment is implemented and secure test storage is available.
3. Confirm that the file is attached to the report.
The selected test file is shown as attached and is associated with the report without exposing it through an unrestricted public link.
The report draft contains the optional dummy evidence attachment.
Test Case 13: Handle Evidence Upload Failure
Verify that the application handles an evidence-upload failure without claiming that the attachment was saved.
Evidence attachment is implemented; the test environment can simulate an upload failure.
File: test-evidence.jpg; Upload result: simulated failure.
3. Simulate or trigger an upload failure in the test environment.
4. Observe the message and attachment state.
The application displays an appropriate error message and does not show the failed file as successfully attached; the reporter can retry or continue without the optional attachment if the UI permits.
No failed upload is represented as saved evidence.
Test Case 14: Submit a Valid Report Successfully
Verify that submitting a report with valid required information saves the report and displays a unique case reference number.
The report service and secure storage are available in the test environment.
Category: Sexual Harassment; Description: Fictional Safe Voice test report; Incident date: 20/10/2026; Time: 14:30; Location: Test Location B.
2. Enter the valid test report information.
The application saves the report and then displays a confirmation message and a unique case reference number.
The test report is stored and has a case reference number.
Test Case 15: Handle Report Submission Failure
Verify that the application displays an error and does not claim successful receipt when the report cannot be saved.
The reporting workflow is available and a save failure can be simulated in the test environment.
Valid fictional report; Save operation: simulated failure.
2. Trigger or simulate a failure when saving the report.
3. Tap the submit control if not already triggered.
An appropriate error message is displayed; no successful-submission confirmation or case reference number is shown unless the report was actually saved.
The report is not marked as successfully received.
Test Case 16: Generate Different References for Separate Reports
Verify that two separately saved reports receive different unique case reference numbers.
The report service is available and two distinct fictional reports can be submitted.
Report A: fictional Domestic Violence report; Report B: fictional Physical Abuse report.
1. Submit Report A with valid test information.
2. Record the reference number displayed after successful saving.
3. Submit Report B with different valid test information.
Both reports are saved successfully and their case reference numbers are different.
Two separate test reports exist with unique references.
Verify that an authorized officer can log in with valid credentials and reach the officer dashboard.
A test officer account is configured and authorized in the test environment.
Valid credentials for the preconfigured test officer account.
2. Enter the valid test officer credentials.
The credentials are accepted and the officer dashboard is displayed.
An authenticated officer session is active.
Test Case 18: Reject Invalid Officer Credentials
Verify that an officer cannot log in using incorrect credentials.
The officer login screen is displayed and a test officer account exists.
2. Enter the test officer identifier and an incorrect password.
Access is denied, an appropriate error message is displayed, and sensitive case information is not shown.
No authenticated officer session is created.
Test Case 19: Reject Empty Officer Login Fields
Verify that the officer login form does not grant access when the required credentials are missing.
The officer login screen is displayed.
3. Attempt to submit the login form.
The application identifies the missing required credentials or otherwise denies login; the officer dashboard is not displayed.
No authenticated officer session is created.
Test Case 20: Prevent Officer Dashboard Access Without Login
Verify that a user who is not authenticated as an officer cannot access the officer dashboard or sensitive case information.
The application is open and no officer is logged in.
Session: logged out; Access attempt: officer section.
1. Launch the application without logging in as an officer.
2. Use any available navigation to attempt to open the officer section.
3. Observe the screen and any case information shown.
The application requires officer authentication and does not display dashboard totals or sensitive case details to the unauthenticated user.
The user remains unauthenticated and case data remains hidden.
Test Case 21: Display Correct Dashboard Case Totals
Verify that the officer dashboard displays accurate totals for assigned, open, resolved, and closed cases.
An authorized officer is logged in and the test database contains cases with known statuses.
Seeded test cases: 1 Assigned, 2 Open, 1 Resolved, 1 Closed.
1. Log in as the authorized test officer.
3. Compare each displayed total with the seeded test data.
The dashboard displays Assigned: 1, Open: 2, Resolved: 1, and Closed: 1 for the test data.
No case data is changed by viewing the dashboard.
Test Case 22: View the All Cases List
Verify that an authorized officer can view the All Cases section and its basic case information.
An authorized officer is logged in and has permission to view the seeded test cases.
At least two fictional cases with reference, category, reported date, status, and permitted access.
3. Inspect the entries displayed in the list.
The list displays cases the officer is authorized to access, with each entry showing the case reference number, incident category, date reported, current status, and an Open Case button.
Test Case 23: Restrict Cases Outside the Officer’s Permissions
Verify that the All Cases list does not expose cases the logged-in officer is not authorized to access.
Two test officers and a fictional case with access restricted to the other officer are configured.
Logged-in user: test officer A; Restricted case: SV-TEST-RESTRICTED.
1. Log in as test officer A.
3. Look for the restricted test case.
4. If a route to the restricted case is available, attempt to open it.
The restricted case is not exposed in the list or its details are denied; the application does not reveal sensitive information to an officer without permission.
The unauthorized officer has not accessed the restricted case.
Test Case 24: Open an Authorized Case
Verify that an authorized officer can open a case and view its permitted incident details.
An authorized officer is logged in and at least one permitted test case exists.
Case: SV-TEST-001; Category: Physical Abuse; fictional description; incident date/time/location and test evidence where available.

The Case Details screen shows available permitted details such as case reference, category, description, incident date and time, incident location, submission date, and any submitted evidence. Reporter identity information is not displayed by default.
The case is viewed without changing its status or content.
Test Case 25: Deny Access to an Unauthorized Case
Verify that an officer cannot open case details for a case they are not permitted to access.
The test environment contains a case for which the logged-in test officer has no access permission.
Logged-in user: test officer A; Restricted case: SV-TEST-RESTRICTED.
1. Log in as test officer A.
2. Attempt to open the restricted case through any available case-list navigation.
The application denies access or omits the case, and does not reveal its incident details or evidence.
No unauthorized case information is displayed.

An authorized officer is viewing a case that is not closed.

The dialog closes and the case
Open; no closure date or time is recorded.

Test Case 28: Handle a Failed Case-Closure Update
Verify that the application does not report successful closure when the case-status update fails to save.
An authorized officer is viewing an open or resolved test case and the test environment can simulate a save failure.
Case: SV-TEST-004; Save operation: simulated failure.
4. Simulate or trigger a failure while saving the status update.
5. Observe the message and case status.
The application displays an appropriate error message and does not show the case as successfully closed; the stored case status remains unchanged.
Test Case 29: Prevent Repeated Closure of an Already Closed Case
Verify that a closed case cannot be closed repeatedly without an appropriate reopening process.
An authorized officer can view a case whose stored status is Closed.
1. Open the already closed test case.
2. Check whether a Close Case action is available.
3. If it is available, attempt to close the case again.
The application does not perform a duplicate closure action; it keeps the case Closed unless an authorized reopening process is used.
The case remains Closed with its existing closure record.
Test Case 30: Refresh Dashboard Totals After Case Closure
Verify that dashboard totals update automatically after a case is successfully closed.
An authorized officer is logged in; dashboard counts are visible; one test case is eligible for closure.
2. Open SV-TEST-006 and close it by confirming the closure dialog.
3. Return to or view the dashboard.
4. Compare the updated summary cards with the new stored statuses.
The Closed total increases by one and the Resolved total decreases by one, while the other totals remain consistent with the stored case statuses.
Dashboard summaries match the updated case statuses.
Test Case 31: Count Each Case Under One Current Status
Verify that dashboard totals reflect each case’s current stored status without counting a case in multiple status categories.
The test database contains cases with known, mutually exclusive current statuses.
Seeded cases: SV-A Assigned; SV-B Open; SV-C Resolved; SV-D Closed.
1. Log in as an authorized officer.
3. Compare the four totals with the four seeded cases.
Each seeded case contributes to only its current status category and the totals match the stored statuses.
No case status is changed by viewing the totals.
